loader_handoff.basis: The X-T4 2.12 loader passes its 0x5d0-byte boot-information block in r1 from 0x10aec; the kernel copies it to 0x82adc. Words 0x00..0x3c are the sixteen GPIO port levels the loader samples at power-on and equal the declared GPIO input. The four flash setup words, ending with the NOR manufacturer byte 0x2c, match that copy in RAM read from a running X-T4 2.12. The cold boot reason and every other word stay synthetic.

power_checksum_registers.basis: Four-byte checksum frames: X-T4 2.12 clocks each power-controller frame as four bytes, most significant first (0x011d4388): a seven-bit register with a write flag, a data word and a checksum byte that brings the byte sum to 0xff (0x011d52fc builds a read). The loader reads the eight-byte settings profile header from registers 31..34 and stores it at boot-information offset 0x148; the board serves the requested profile header there. Startup writes 0x0100 to register 18 and the settings and power code write registers 2, 31..34 and 39 back, so these are stored words. The stock loader that runs from flash before the kernel writes 0x7f00 to register 17, the value the firmware's power-register cache holds, so register 17 is declared a stored word too. The firmware reads register 0 through XOR 0x3407 (0x0225bdb0, 0x0225ef70); 0x3007 leaves only bit 0x400 active, which startup (0x01291324) needs to continue a boot with reason 4. Registers 2, 3, 4, 5, 14, 17, 29, 30, 39, 47..50, 64, 65, 67, 71, 72, 111..114 and 118..121 are the last values in the firmware's power-register cache, and 37, 38, 69 and 70 the values in its power-register shadow, in RAM of a running X-T4 2.12 read in USB service mode. Registers 35 (low) and 36 (high) are a seconds-since-2000 clock (0x011d708c), declared stopped at zero. The clock is set by staging the seconds in registers 29 (low) and 30 (high) and committing with 0x0202 set in register 39 (0x011d70c4); that law is not modeled for this body, so leaving the first-start pages with BACK refuses at the register 29 write. Physical values at power-on are not measured.

stabilizer_link.basis: In-body stabilizer controller on SPI2, as its link behaves: the camera powers it with GPIO outputs 0.12 and 1.14 (powered while both are high), pulses its reset on 12.6 (high, then low releases it), selects it with 12.3 (active low) and exchanges four-byte frames of eight-bit words, most significant first. The controller reports on pad 0.4, which reads its GPIO input level (high) while the controller is unpowered or held in reset: the pad goes low once the controller has booted and high after the first frame of the link. The boot delay, 10 ms at 54 MHz, is declared, not measured. No command reply data is declared, so every reply carries data 0, which the periodic status traffic at the shooting screen (status id 0x29 every 40 ms, ids 0x2a and 0x11a) accepts.

geometry.basis: 128 KiB erase sectors and 256-byte pages of the MT35XU512ABA; erase and page timing are declared virtual inputs.

serial_flash.basis: The X-T4 NOR is a Micron MT35XU512ABA, 64 MiB, JEDEC ID 2c 5b 1a. The model returns the identity bytes in one data word, first byte lowest, so the declared word is 0x1a5b2c: the stock loader takes the low byte as the manufacturer and stores 0x2c, the manufacturer the firmware reads from boot information offset 0x5cc. Erase and page timing are declared virtual inputs.

gpio_input.basis: GPIO port levels the X-T4 2.12 loader sampled at a power-on of a running X-T4 (boot-information words 0x00..0x3c of its kernel copy in RAM), taken with the service-entry keys held. Port 0 bits 0 and 1 (shutter S1/S2, active low as on the X-T3) are declared released. The firmware selects the firmware-update start from these levels (DISP/BACK held at power-on); all-zero levels read every active-low key as held and start it. UP is GPIO 7.11 active low in the X-T4 2.12 key scanner table; that sample reads it low, held for service entry, so bit 11 of port 7 is declared released too.

gpio_interrupts.basis: Stabilizer ready pad 0.4 on two level-sensitive interrupt inputs: GIC 171 is asserted while the pad is low (the controller has booted after its reset release) and GIC 155 while it is high (the controller has answered the first frame of its link). The camera waits on each in turn while it opens the link.
